findings.obligation: Falsifier: 'Publishing with the round's token (cancelled row missing)'; decision: publish with CancellationToken.None so a cancelled round still writes its row
findings.observation: Non-blocking, unobservable falsifier. The cancelled row asserts 'Assert.That(entry.Cancelled, Is.EqualTo(cancelled)' but a handler handed the cancelled token still writes the row: DomainEventDispatcher.InvokeHandlerSafely only awaits handler.HandleAsync(domainEvent, cancellationToken) and RefreshLogService.LogRefreshAsync(RefreshLog) takes no token. Token misuse named in the design cannot turn this row red; only mapping or missing-handler defects can.
findings.remediation: Design: restate the falsifier as mapping or missing handler for the cancelled row, or declare handler-side honouring of the token as an obligation. Oracle: no change required before craft.
